I’m excited to share that The Kasari Nexus is available for people to download advance copies from NetGalley through 4/5. Below is a link and the NetGalley widget that will automatically approve you to get a review copy of your own, once you’ve signed up for NetGalley.

Kasari Nexus, The

https://www.netgalley.com/widget/open?widget_id=83457_81285_145505858756ba6e9b84fff_9781503933538_US

NetGalley is a secure digital platform that allows us to share digital review copies with NetGalley’s community of over 175,000 professional readers — reviewers, bloggers, media professionals, booksellers, librarians, and educators. It has grown steadily in size and influence, as many reviewers have migrated from paperback to digital ARCs. NetGalley is one tool we use to increase our digital outreach to important reviewers and tastemakers and drive customers to leave reviews for a book on your Amazon detail page on its on-sale date.

Please leave a review on Amazon.com and Goodreads once you’ve finished reading, but please make sure to include the disclaimer “I received a free, advance copy of this book from the publisher via NetGalley in exchange for my unbiased review” to the end of your text.

PDF copies reviewers download will expire for reviewers 55 days after a user downloads it. Kindle review copies that are downloaded by reviewers do not expire, but can’t be downloaded for free after the publication date.

How you use NetGalley

NetGalley accounts are free for anyone to create. The reviewer must have and be logged in to a NetGalley account to request and download titles from the site. If are new to NetGalley, you can visit NetGalley Reading How-To page for more information.

comments.html: Hello Richard, I would like to add one of your books to the recommended list of books by other authors, that I have inside the first book of my Synchronicity War series. Would you be willing to insert a recommendation for one of my books at the front of one of yours with a clickable link? You can reach me at [email removed].

replies.author: Richard Phillips
replies.html: Thank you very much. If I was still self-published I would be happy to. However, the terms of my contract with my publisher specify that only they can make any changes or editions to the books that they publish. I wish you the very best with your marketing efforts. Richard
